groups.defect: In DualWriterMode3.Create, the goroutine passes the same `obj` pointer to Legacy.Create after Storage.Create has used it, while that object may also be returned or serialized. This allows concurrent mutation and a data race. The fix is to pass obj.DeepCopyObject() into the goroutine.

answer.reasoning: Both suggestions point at the same code: Create, line 55, inside the 42-59 range. They report the same defect. The shared `obj` pointer, which Storage.Create may have changed, goes to Legacy.Create in a goroutine while the caller may be serializing the same object. Both propose the same fix, DeepCopyObject. The judges disagreed only on needsUnifiedComment. s_4ee7f335 adds that Unified Storage metadata could reach Legacy. That is another consequence of the same shared or mutated pointer, and the same single edit at the same place fixes it. It is not a separate defect needing its own fix, so one member's comment covers the group. needsUnifiedComment is false.
